title: Super Supportive · Episode 1: Someone Who Answers
description: Two weeks after the disaster, young Alden receives a visitor. A small, unexpected conversation gives him something he has been missing: someone who takes his questions seriously.

sources.title: Super Supportive — Sleyca
sources.note: Based on the user-supplied EPUB: chapter TWO: Mistakes through the scar exchange; brief memories from ONE: The Boy in the Bubble. Not an official translation. No permission or public-domain status inferred from web availability.

planning.voiceReason: David selected intimate character drama and quiet local payoffs, welcoming source-supported perspective shifts.
planning.sourceBoundary: Chapter 2 opening through “It doesn’t hurt much anymore.” Brief rescue recollections from chapter 1; no later explanation of the disaster.
planning.earlyCare: Alden keeps Wummy close and wants adults to tell him the truth.
planning.desire: Be taken seriously and learn what happened.
planning.obstacle: Adults avoid his questions, while Hannah struggles with guilt.
planning.dramaticChange: Alden discovers he can speak comfortably to Hannah; she accepts his unusual curiosity.
planning.payoff: Hannah agrees to ask about the shrapnel and takes his scar seriously.
planning.newUncertainty: Will she answer the painful question about his parents?
planning.englishNarrationPurpose: None. All story beats and choices in Mandarin.
choicesAndCallbacks: Look out the window / at Wummy: different private observations, rejoin visitor.
Quiet nod / attentive nod: different acknowledgment of consent; rejoin seated conversation.
Ask what the fragment was / say he never saw it: distinct opening question, rejoin explanation.
Invite her to see scar / describe its color: distinct exchange, rejoin her enthusiasm. No persistent variables.
sceneActivities: Alden remains seated/reclining at the bed; Hannah first stands at a distance, sits only after his nod; restrained gestures accompany the metal size explanation.
Stillness during listening is intentional; no compulsory walk or training loop.

signatures.Alden: Short direct questions, concrete childlike curiosity, watchful stillness and rare pleased expression.
signatures.Hannah: Hesitant openings, permission before approaching, matter-of-fact answers; warmth offsets guarded guilt.

planning.directing: Shared pair through ordinary replies; Hannah listener at Alden’s unusual request; Alden listener for her offer and enthusiastic scar response; aftermath persists until Continue.

planning.pinyinReview: Reviewed full sentences and chunks; corrected contextual polyphones and neutral tones.

continuation.end: Hannah agrees to ask about the shrapnel and admires Alden’s scar; he feels heard. The cause of his parents’ deaths is not yet explained.
continuation.note: The bubble explanation and truth about the disaster; allow grief and aftermath when extending boundary deliberately.
continuity: Alden remains a child in hospital; design A is the later teenage reference.
Wummy was rescued with him. His parents are dead; he still seeks the full explanation.
Hannah has consent to visit, has promised to ask about the saw fragment, and has admired his purple scar.
No persistent branch changes to source events.
Intimate character drama, quiet local payoffs, occasional source-supported perspective shifts.

intro.title: Do you want to see my scar?

notice: A private Mandarin learning adaptation of Sleyca’s Super Supportive. Dialogue is simplified and brief choices rejoin the novel’s events. This opening takes place during Alden’s childhood and includes bereavement and recollections of injury.
